definition_zh: 会议记录；会议纪要；分钟（minute 的复数）
definition_en: the official written record of what was said and decided at a meeting, or the plural of the time unit minute
core_image: 会议桌旁，有人低头把发言用很小的字记在纸角上
scene: 董事会结束后，秘书把讨论要点整理成文件。The secretary typed up the minutes right after the board meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 minutes 是「会议记录」（第 1 个义项：会议发言与决定的正式书面记录）；句意：董事会结束后，秘书马上把会议记录打了出来。

derivatives.zh: 细节；琐事（拉丁语「微小之物」的复数形式）
极小的；细微的（与「分钟」同源，读作 /maɪˈnjuːt/）

senses.title: The written record of a meeting
senses.definition: the official notes of what was said and decided at a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 对会议发言与决定所作的正式书面记录
senses.example: Please read the minutes before the next meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 请在下次会议前阅读会议记录。
senses.why: Medieval Latin minuta meant a short note, and the small notes taken at a meeting became the minutes.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 minuta 指简短的札记；会议上记下的「小字条」后来固定成会议记录。

senses.title: A sixtieth of an hour
senses.definition: each of the sixty equal parts of an hour, used as a unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 一小时的六十分之一，用作时间单位
senses.example: The talk lasts about twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这场讲话大约持续二十分钟。
senses.why: Latin pars minuta prima, the first small part, cut the hour into small pieces and gave minute its time sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pars minuta prima（第一个小部分）把一小时切成小份，分钟的时间义由此长出来。

senses.title: A brief memorandum
senses.definition: a short written note recording an agreement or a transaction
senses.definitionCN: 记录某项协议或某项交易的简短书面札记
senses.example: The parties signed a minute of the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 各方签署了一份协议备忘录。
senses.why: The same small-note sense survives in legal and business use for a short memorandum.
senses.whyCN: 「小札记」这一层意思在法律与商务里保留下来，用来指简短的备忘录。

senses.title: To record in the minutes
senses.definition: to write something down in the official record of a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 把某事写进会议的正式记录
senses.example: The objection was minuted by the clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 书记员把这项异议记入了会议记录。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to minute something is to put it into the small notes.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：把某事「记进小字条」，就是记入会议记录。

intro.en: Minutes comes from Latin minutus, small, through the medieval use of minuta for a short note or draft.
intro.cn: minutes 来自拉丁语 minutus（小的），经由中世纪拉丁语 minuta（简短札记、草稿）进入英语。

items.en: Minuere means to make smaller, and minutus means small.
items.cn: minuere 意为使变小，minutus 意为小的。

items.en: Pars minuta prima, the first small part, names a sixtieth of an hour.
items.cn: pars minuta prima（第一个小部分）指一小时的六十分之一，即分钟。

items.en: Minuta names a short draft or note written down for later use.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 minuta 指供日后使用的简短草稿或札记。

items.en: Menu and minute carry the sense of something small and finely detailed.
items.cn: menu 与 minute 都带有「细小、详尽」的意思。

items.en: The small notes taken during a meeting are called its minutes.
items.cn: 十五世纪起，会议当场记下的「小字条」被称为 minutes。

items.en: The plural minutes becomes the standard name for the official record.
items.cn: 复数形式 minutes 成为正式记录的固定名称。

note.en: Minutes belongs to the small-note family of minute, minutiae and minuet, and it sits near the record words of a meeting.
note.cn: minutes 属于「小札记」词族，与 minute、minutiae、minuet 同源，也与会议记录类词相邻。

entries.definition: the singular of minutes, and a unit of time
entries.definitionCN: minutes 的单数形式，也指分钟

entries.definition: a slow elegant dance of the seventeenth century
entries.definitionCN: 十七世纪的一种优雅慢舞，经法语 menuet（细小的舞步）同样源自 minutus

entries.definition: a written account of facts or events
the formal record of a meeting or a hearing
entries.definitionCN: 会议记录；诉讼程序记录

normalIntro.en: Minutes are the small notes of a meeting: the word itself comes from Latin minutus, small.
normalIntro.cn: minutes 是会议上的「小字条」：词本身就来自拉丁语 minutus（小的）。

normal.en: To take the minutes means to write the official record.
normal.cn: take the minutes 就是做会议记录。

normal.en: The minutes of the meeting are approved at the next one.
normal.cn: 会议记录通常在下次会议上批准。

normal.en: Minute and minutes both come from Latin minutus, small.
normal.cn: minute 与 minutes 都来自拉丁语 minutus（小的）。

normal.en: A minute is a small part of an hour, and sixty of them make one hour.
normal.cn: 一分钟是一小时的一个小部分，六十分钟为一小时。

normal.en: Compare memorandum: a memo is an internal note, the minutes are the formal record.
normal.cn: 对比 memorandum：memo 多为内部便条，minutes 是正式记录。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk writing tiny letters in the corner of a page.
abstract.cn: 想象书记员在纸角写下很小的字。

abstract.en: Picture the clock face cut into sixty small slices.
abstract.cn: 想象表盘被切成六十个小格。

abstract.en: Picture a short note pinned to a contract.
abstract.cn: 想象一张短笺钉在合同上。

examples.en: The chair asked the secretary to take the minutes.
examples.cn: 主席请秘书做会议记录。

examples.en: We have only ten minutes before the next session.
examples.cn: 下一场开始前我们只有十分钟。

examples.en: The minutes were circulated to all board members.
examples.cn: 会议记录已传发给全体董事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「minutes」读近「迷你次」——会议记录要像「迷你」一样短小，每次开会都记一份；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 minuere（使变小）→ minutus（小的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 minuta（简短札记）→ 英语 minute / minutes；核心义「小」：小札记成了会议记录，一小份时间成了分钟。

sensesIntro.en: Minutes first names the small notes of a meeting, then the time unit, the short memorandum, and finally the act of recording.
sensesIntro.cn: minutes 先指会议上的小札记，再指时间单位「分钟」、简短备忘录，最后指记入会议记录的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small handwriting in the corner of a meeting page.
core.cn: 核心意象：会议纸页角上用很小的字写下的笔记。

branches.en: The meeting record is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 会议记录是今天最主要的义项。

branches.en: The time unit comes from the first small part of an hour.
branches.cn: 时间单位来自「一小时的第一个小部分」。

branches.en: A short memorandum keeps the older note sense.
branches.cn: 简短备忘录保留了更早的「札记」义。

branches.en: The record and the act of recording are two sides of one practice.
branches.cn: 记录本身与记录动作是同一做法的两面。

branches.en: Both a minute and a memorandum are short written notes.
branches.cn: 会议记录与备忘录都是简短的书面札记。

intro.en: Minutes is built on Latin minutus, small, with a family that includes minute, minutiae and minimum.
intro.cn: minutes 建立在拉丁语 minutus（小的）之上，同族词包括 minute、minutiae 与 minimum。

latinIntro.en: Latin minuere means to lessen and minutus means small; medieval minuta names a short draft.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minuere 意为减少，minutus 意为小的；中世纪 minuta 指简短草稿。

items.example: Minuere gives the idea of making small.
items.exampleCN: minuere 提供「使变小」的概念。

items.example: Minutus is the source of minute.
items.exampleCN: minutus 是 minute 的来源。

items.example: Minuta is the small note behind the minutes.
items.exampleCN: minuta 就是会议记录背后那张「小字条」。

items.meaning: the sixtieth part of an hour
items.example: A minute is a small part of an hour.
items.exampleCN: 一分钟是一小时的一个小部分。

items.meaning: the written record of a meeting
items.example: Minutes is the official record of a meeting.
items.exampleCN: minutes 是会议的正式记录。

items.example: The prefix mini- marks something small.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mini- 标记「小」的事物。

items.example: Minimum keeps the sense of the smallest amount.
items.exampleCN: minimum 保留「最小量」的意思。

items.example: Minor comes from the same Latin root.
items.exampleCN: minor 来自同一个拉丁语词根。

items.example: Diminish reaches English through Old French.
items.exampleCN: diminish 经由古法语进入英语。

definition_zh: 营业额；人员流动率；周转率
definition_en: the total amount of money a business receives in a period, or the rate at which staff or stock is replaced
core_image: 货物从货架这头转到那头，钱在柜台里转了一圈又回来
scene: 季度结算时，财务经理报出公司的销售总额。The finance manager reported the company turnover for the quarter.
sceneCN: 这里 turnover 是「营业额」（第 1 个义项：一定时期内的销售总额）；句意：季度结算时，财务经理报出了公司的营业额。

pos.zh: 营业额；人员流动率；周转率

derivatives.zh: 翻倒；推翻（over 与 turn 换位构成的近亲）
好转；周转时间（turn 与 around 构成的复合词）

senses.title: The money taken in a period
senses.definition: the total amount of money a business receives from sales in a period
senses.definitionCN: 企业在某一时期内通过销售收到的款项总额
senses.example: Annual turnover rose by a fifth last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年年营业额上升了五分之一。
senses.why: The phrasal verb turn over means to hand money across a counter, so turnover became the money that passes through a business.
senses.whyCN: 短语动词 turn over 指把钱从柜台上转手；流经企业的钱于是被称为 turnover，即营业额。

senses.title: The rate at which staff are replaced
senses.definition: the proportion of employees who leave and are replaced during a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内离职并被替换的员工所占的比例
senses.example: High turnover is costly for the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 人员流动率高对公司来说代价很大。
senses.why: People turn over in a job as posts are vacated and refilled, so the same word names staff replacement.
senses.whyCN: 员工像岗位上的「翻转」一样离开又被补上，同一个词就用来指人员流动率。

senses.title: The rate at which stock is sold
senses.definition: the speed at which goods are sold and replaced in a shop or store
senses.definitionCN: 商店里的货物卖出并被补货的速度
senses.example: Fast turnover keeps the stock fresh.
senses.exampleCN: 周转快能让存货保持新鲜。
senses.why: Stock turns over as it is sold and replaced, which gives the stock sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 存货卖出又补货，像在货架上「翻转」一轮，于是有了存货周转的意思。

senses.title: A loss of possession in sport
senses.definition: the act of losing the ball to the other team in a game
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中把球丢给对方球队的行为
senses.example: The coach blamed the turnover for the defeat.
senses.exampleCN: 教练把失利归咎于那次丢球。
senses.why: A team turns the ball over to the other side, so a lost possession is a turnover.
senses.whyCN: 球队把球「转交」给对方，丢掉的球权就叫 turnover。

senses.title: A folded pastry
senses.definition: a small pie made by folding pastry over a fruit or meat filling
senses.definitionCN: 把面皮翻转折叠、包住水果或肉馅的小点心
senses.example: She bought an apple turnover at the bakery.
senses.exampleCN: 她在面包店买了一只苹果酥饼。
senses.why: Pastry is turned over and folded around the filling, which names the little pie.
senses.whyCN: 面皮被「翻转」折起来包住馅料，这种小点心因此得名。

intro.en: Turnover is the English compound of turn and over; turn goes back through Old French to Latin tornare, to turn on a lathe.
intro.cn: turnover 是 turn 与 over 构成的英语复合词；turn 经古法语可追溯到拉丁语 tornare，意为在车床上转动。

items.en: Tornare means to turn on a lathe, from tornus, a lathe.
items.cn: tornare 意为在车床上转动，源于 tornus（车床）。

items.en: Torner carries the verb into French with the sense of turning.
items.cn: torner 把这个动词带入法语，表示转动。

items.en: Turn enters English and names a circular movement.
items.cn: 十三世纪起，turn 进入英语，指圆周式的转动。

items.en: Over adds the sense of moving across or from one side to the other.
items.cn: over 增添「越过、从一侧到另一侧」的意思。

items.en: Turnover names the amount of money taken in a period.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，turnover 指一段时期内进账的金额。

items.en: The word also names the replacement of staff and the rotation of stock.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词也指人员替换与存货周转。

note.en: Turnover is the compound of turn and over, close to turn over, overturn and turnaround, and to the revenue words of accounting.
note.cn: turnover 是 turn 与 over 的复合词，与 turn over、overturn、turnaround 形近，也与会计里的收入类词相邻。

entries.definition: to flip something or hand it across
to tip over or reverse a decision
a complete change for the better
the total value of goods sold
money left after costs are paid

normalIntro.en: Turnover is turn plus over: money, staff and stock all turn over and come round again.
normalIntro.cn: turnover 是 turn 加 over：钱、人和货都在「转一圈」，然后又回来。

normal.en: Turnover is the money that turns over in a business during a period.
normal.cn: turnover 是一段时期内企业里「转一圈」的钱，即营业额。

normal.en: Staff turnover measures how many people leave and are replaced.
normal.cn: staff turnover 衡量有多少人离开又被替换。

normal.en: Stock turnover measures how fast goods are sold.
normal.cn: stock turnover 衡量货物卖得多快。

normal.en: Turn over a page and you move it to the other side; turn over money and it changes hands.
normal.cn: turn over a page 是把书页翻到另一面；turn over money 是让钱转手。

normal.en: Compare revenue: revenue is accounting income, turnover is the sales total.
normal.cn: 对比 revenue：revenue 是会计口径的收入，turnover 是销售总额。

abstract.en: Picture a coin spinning on a counter and coming back.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币在柜台上转了一圈又回来。

abstract.en: Picture a revolving door with people going out and in.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇旋转门，人不断走出又走进。

abstract.en: Picture boxes sliding off a shelf and new ones taking their place.
abstract.cn: 想象箱子滑下货架，新箱子补上位置。

examples.en: The firm has an annual turnover of about two million pounds.
examples.cn: 这家公司的年营业额约为两百万英镑。

examples.en: Staff turnover has fallen since the new pay scheme.
examples.cn: 自新薪酬方案实施以来，员工流动率下降了。

examples.en: An apple turnover was warming in the bakery window.
examples.cn: 面包店的橱窗里，一只苹果酥饼正热着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「turnover」读近「腾欧沃」——货物「腾」出去、人「挪」走、钱「转」回来，营业额与流动率都在其中；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 turn（转动，源自拉丁语 tornare「在车床上转」）+ over（越过、翻过）→ turn over（翻转；移交）→ turnover（流转的总额：营业额、人员流动率、周转率）。

sensesIntro.en: Turnover starts as money that turns over in trade, then extends to staff and stock that are replaced, to a lost ball, and to a folded pastry.
sensesIntro.cn: turnover 从买卖中「转一圈」的钱开始，再扩展到被替换的员工与存货、丢掉的球权，以及折叠而成的酥饼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: goods and money turning over and coming back round.
core.cn: 核心意象：货物与钱转了一圈又回来。

branches.en: The sales total is the accounting core.
branches.cn: 销售总额是会计上的核心义。

branches.en: Staff replacement extends the turning image to people.
branches.cn: 人员替换把「翻转」的意象扩展到人。

branches.en: Stock rotation extends it to goods on a shelf.
branches.cn: 存货周转把意象扩展到货架上的货物。

branches.en: A lost ball is a turn of possession to the other side.
branches.cn: 丢球就是把球权转交给对方。

branches.en: A folded pastry is pastry turned over on itself.
branches.cn: 折叠酥饼就是把面皮翻转包起来。

intro.en: Turnover is an English compound of turn and over; turn itself goes back through Old French to Latin tornare.
intro.cn: turnover 是 turn 与 over 构成的英语复合词；turn 经古法语可追溯到拉丁语 tornare。

latinIntro.en: Latin tornare means to turn on a lathe, from tornus, a lathe; over is Germanic and adds the sense of across.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tornare 意为在车床上转动，源于 tornus（车床）；over 属日耳曼语，增添「越过」之义。

items.example: Turn names the circular movement.
items.exampleCN: turn 指圆周式的转动。

items.meaning: across, from one side to the other
items.example: Over adds the crossing movement.
items.exampleCN: over 增添越过、横跨的动作。

items.meaning: to flip something or hand it over
items.example: Turn over joins the two halves.
items.exampleCN: turn over 把两半合在一起。

items.meaning: the money a business takes in a period
items.example: Turnover is the money that passes through.
items.exampleCN: turnover 是流经企业的钱。

items.example: Overturn swaps the two parts.
items.exampleCN: overturn 把两部分换了位置。

items.example: Turnaround adds around to turn.
items.exampleCN: turnaround 在 turn 后加上 around。

items.meaning: a gate that turns to let one person through
items.example: Turnstile joins turn and stile.
items.exampleCN: turnstile 由 turn 与 stile 构成。

items.meaning: ready to use as soon as it is handed over
items.meaningCN: 交钥匙的；可直接使用的
items.example: Turnkey describes a project handed over ready to use.
items.exampleCN: turnkey 形容交付即可使用的项目。

definition_zh: 利益相关方；股东；持股人
definition_en: a person or group with an interest in a business or a decision, or a person who holds a stake
core_image: 几个人从不同方向握住同一口锅的锅柄
scene: 工厂要搬迁，管理层先征询受影响各方的意见。Before moving the factory, the firm consulted every stakeholder.
sceneCN: 这里 stakeholder 是「利益相关方」（第 1 个义项：与企业经营有利害关系的个人或群体）；句意：搬迁工厂之前，公司征询了每一位利益相关方的意见。

pos.zh: 利益相关方；股东；持股人

derivatives.zh: 股东（持有公司股份的人）
多方利益相关者参与的

senses.title: A party with an interest in a business
senses.definition: a person or group that is affected by or has an interest in how a business is run
senses.definitionCN: 受企业经营影响、或对经营方式有利益的个人或群体
senses.example: Customers and employees are both stakeholders in the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 客户与员工都是这家公司的利益相关方。
senses.why: A stake is something risked or invested, so a stakeholder is anyone who holds a share of the outcome.
senses.whyCN: stake 是押进去、投进去的东西，所以 stakeholder 就是「握有一份结果」的人，即利益相关方。

senses.title: A holder of shares
senses.definition: a person who owns shares in a company
senses.example: The largest stakeholder holds a third of the shares.
senses.exampleCN: 最大的持股人持有三分之一的股份。
senses.why: The word can be read literally as the holder of a stake, that is, of a financial share.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以照字面读成「握着 stake 的人」；当 stake 指股份时，它就是持股人。

senses.title: The keeper of the bets
senses.definition: the person who holds the money wagered until the result is known
senses.definitionCN: 在结果揭晓之前替人保管赌注的人
senses.example: The stakeholder kept the wagers until the race ended.
senses.exampleCN: 赌注保管人一直保管着赌金，直到比赛结束。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: in a wager the stakeholder holds the stakes for the two sides.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：赌局里由 stakeholder 替双方保管赌注。

senses.title: A party affected by a decision
senses.definition: a group or person whose interests are affected by a project or a public decision
senses.definitionCN: 利益受某个项目或某项公共决策影响的群体或个人
senses.example: Residents became stakeholders in the new transport plan.
senses.exampleCN: 居民成了新交通计划的相关方。
senses.why: Modern policy use widens the betting image to anyone who holds a stake in a public decision.
senses.whyCN: 现代政策用法把「押注」的意象放大：凡在公共决策里有一份利害的人，都是相关方。

intro.en: Stakeholder joins stake, a pointed post and later a wager, to holder, one who holds; the betting sense came first.
intro.cn: stakeholder 由 stake（削尖的木桩，后指赌注）与 holder（持有者）组合而成，最早出现的是赌局义。

items.en: Staca names a pointed wooden post driven into the ground.
items.cn: staca 指削尖后打进地里的木桩。

items.en: Healdan means to hold or keep something in ones charge.
items.cn: healdan 意为握住、保管某物。

items.en: Stake also names the money put at risk in a wager.
items.cn: 十四世纪起，stake 也指押在赌局里的钱。

items.en: A stakeholder is first the person who holds the bets.
items.cn: stakeholder 最初指替人保管赌注的人。

items.en: Business writing adopts the word for anyone with an interest in a firm.
items.cn: 二十世纪商业写作借用该词，指与企业有利害关系的人。

items.en: The word now covers staff, customers, suppliers and communities.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖员工、客户、供应商与社区。

note.en: Stakeholder joins stake and holder, next to shareholder and stockholder, and it sits near the party words of business.
note.cn: stakeholder 由 stake 与 holder 组合，与 shareholder、stockholder 形近，也与商业里的「当事方」类词相邻。

entries.definition: a post, a bet, or a share
an owner of shares in a company
a person who puts money into a business
one of the sides in an agreement or dispute
a person who takes part in something

normalIntro.en: Stakeholder is literally the holder of a stake: a share, a bet, or an interest in a decision.
normalIntro.cn: stakeholder 字面上就是「握着 stake 的人」：那份 stake 可以是股份、赌注，也可以是对某项决策的利害。

normal.en: A stake is a share you have put into something.
normal.cn: stake 是你投进某事的份额。

normal.en: A holder is the person who keeps or owns it.
normal.cn: holder 是保管或拥有它的人。

normal.en: In a bet, the stakeholder holds the money until the result.
normal.cn: 赌局里，stakeholder 在结果出来前保管赌注。

normal.en: In business, a stakeholder holds an interest in the firm.
normal.cn: 在商业中，stakeholder 持有企业的一份利益。

normal.en: Compare shareholder: a shareholder owns shares, a stakeholder may only be affected.
normal.cn: 对比 shareholder：股东持有股份，利益相关方可能只是受影响。

abstract.en: Picture several hands on the rim of one pot.
abstract.cn: 想象几只手同时握住同一口锅的锅柄。

abstract.en: Picture a person holding a sealed envelope of bets.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人捧着一只封好的赌注信封。

abstract.en: Picture neighbours gathered around a notice of a new road.
abstract.cn: 想象邻居们围在一块新道路告示前。

examples.en: Every stakeholder was invited to the consultation.
examples.cn: 每一位利益相关方都获邀参加咨询。

examples.en: The plan must balance the interests of all stakeholders.
examples.cn: 该计划必须平衡所有相关方的利益。

examples.en: A shareholder is one kind of stakeholder in a company.
examples.cn: 股东是公司的一类利益相关方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「stakeholder」谐音近似「steak holder」——分牛排时人人有份，人人都是利益相关方；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 stake（木桩；赌注；股份，源自古英语 staca）+ holder（持有者，源自古英语 healdan）→ stakeholder：先指替人保管赌注的人，再指持股人，最后指利益相关方。

sensesIntro.en: Stakeholder begins as the keeper of a wager, narrows to the holder of shares, and widens to anyone with an interest in a firm or a decision.
sensesIntro.cn: stakeholder 最初指赌注保管人，后缩小为持股人，再扩大为对企业或决策有利益的任何一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands holding the same pot from different sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：几只手从不同方向握住同一口锅。

branches.en: The business sense is the everyday one today.
branches.cn: 企业语境是今天最日常的义项。

branches.en: The shareholding sense reads stake as a financial share.
branches.cn: 持股义把 stake 读作金融股份。

branches.en: The betting keeper is the oldest recorded sense.
branches.cn: 赌注保管人是最早有记录的义项。

branches.en: An owner of shares is a stakeholder in the strict financial sense.
branches.cn: 股份持有人在严格的财务意义上就是利益相关方。

branches.en: A firm and a public project both have parties with stakes.
branches.cn: 企业与公共项目都有握着一份利害的当事方。

intro.en: Stakeholder is an English compound of stake and holder; both halves are Germanic rather than Latin.
intro.cn: stakeholder 是 stake 与 holder 构成的英语复合词，两半都属日耳曼语，而非拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here: stake goes back to Old English staca and holder to healdan, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源：stake 源自古英语 staca，holder 源自古英语 healdan，所以拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.meaning: a post, a bet, or a share
items.example: Stake carries the post and the wager senses.
items.exampleCN: stake 同时带有木桩与赌注两层意思。

items.meaning: to keep something in the hand or in charge
items.example: Hold is the verb behind holder.
items.exampleCN: hold 是 holder 背后的动词。

items.example: Holder is formed with the agent suffix -er.
items.exampleCN: holder 由表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成。

items.meaning: a share or property that is owned
items.example: Holding names what is held.
items.exampleCN: holding 指被持有的东西。

items.example: Stakeholder joins the two halves.
items.exampleCN: stakeholder 把两半合在一起。

items.example: Shareholder swaps stake for share.
items.exampleCN: shareholder 把 stake 换成了 share。

items.meaning: an owner of stock, in American use
items.example: Stockholder is the American twin.
items.exampleCN: stockholder 是美式说法里的同义形式。

items.meaning: to mark an area with stakes, or to watch a place
items.example: Stake out returns to the wooden post.
items.exampleCN: stake out 回到「木桩」的本义。
